name: Hardware Verified
status: trial: Hardware Verified is a trial feature. It may change or be removed.
description: Arcade games on the MisterZine release tracker where the real thing was consulted while building the core for this board: a board in hand (owned or borrowed), its schematics, or decaps of its own chips, with logic analyzer or scope captures, PAL/PROM dumps or a published write-up as the evidence. Using another project's hardware-derived chip models does not count by itself; the author of this core has to have done the checking against this board. Verified means the real hardware was consulted, not that every behavior was tested. Positive only: a game without an entry means nothing. Entries are curated by hand from public, checkable evidence, from the core's author or anyone else who did or documented the work, and each lists the links it rests on.

fields.title: the game's title on the tracker when the entry was made (informational; titles can change, the key does not)
fields.rbfs: the shipped core file name(s) without the date stamp and .rbf extension (data.json core)
fields.setnames: the MAME set name(s) of the row (data.json sn)
fields.granted: the day the entry was added, YYYY-MM-DD
fields.proposed_by: who proposed the entry (anyone; 'misterzine' for entries added by the tracker itself)
fields.reason: what the evidence shows, in plain words
fields.links: the evidence: public pages citing the concrete hardware work (the core's author's or anyone else's)

badges.reason: James Sweet built the core from the Super Breakout schematics, naming its signals as drawn there (256H*, VBLANK*, COMP SYNC*). The ball position counters reproduce the pairs of 74LS163s at board locations R5/R6, P5/P6 and N5/N6.

badges.title: Donkey Kong 3
badges.reason: gaz68 built the core chip by chip from the Donkey Kong 3 schematics, such as the 74LS139 at 3B and the 74LS138s at 2A, 3A, 4E and 4F in the address decoder. The source cites the schematics' CL1 palette link and notes a signal at 2K that goes nowhere on the schematic.

badges.title: Mr. Do!
badges.reason: Darren Olafson modelled the Mr. Do! video hardware from its schematics. The source cites schematic signal names such as VADLAY and the pad counter, and names chips by board position, such as the G9 mux and the F8 and G8 counters.

badges.title: Inferno
badges.reason: The repository ships Williams' Inferno manual with its schematics. birdybro's commit states that the core's colour lookup table is derived from the schematics, the RGB circuit being the same across Inferno, Joust 2, Mystic Marathon and Turkey Shoot.

badges.title: Joust 2 - Survival of the Fittest
badges.reason: Joust 2 runs on the same Williams second-generation board as Inferno, and the Inferno schematics ship in this core's doc folder. The colour lookup table is derived from the schematics; birdybro notes the RGB circuit is the same across Inferno, Joust 2, Mystic Marathon and Turkey Shoot.

badges.title: Mystic Marathon
badges.reason: The core's doc folder holds Williams' Mystic Marathon drawing set (16-3008-103) and its RGB circuit, and birdybro's release commit updates the colour lookup table from the RGB schematics, crediting Kitrinx. Dar's source also names board chips, such as the 74LS85 at IC79 that sets the background colour bank.

badges.title: Turkey Shoot - The Day They Took Over
badges.reason: Turkey Shoot runs on the same Williams second-generation board as Inferno, whose schematics ship with the Inferno core. birdybro's commit there states that the colour lookup table these cores share is derived from the schematics, with the same RGB circuit on Turkey Shoot, Mystic Marathon, Joust 2 and Inferno.

badges.title: Victory Road
badges.reason: Victory Road runs on the same three SNK boards as the JAMMA Ikari Warriors (CPU A6002UP03-02, middle A5004UP02-02, video A5004UP01-02), with a Y8950 in place of the second YM3526. The shared core converts the A5004-1 PAL from a JEDEC dump of Ikari Warriors' own PAL, builds the logic from the board's TTL chips and ships an edited Ikari Warriors schematic.

badges.title: Psychic 5
badges.reason: Raki drew KiCad schematics of the Psychic 5 CPU and video boards and ships them with the core, whose video logic names chips by board position, such as the LS74 at 7H. He also notes checking an original Japanese PCB, which carries a 512K sound ROM where MAME assumes 256K.

badges.title: Super Locomotive
badges.reason: Raki ships a KiCad schematic of the Super Locomotive board together with sigrok logic analyzer captures of its 74LS321 clock chip and its PA-5016 and PA-5017 PALs. The RTL points to the LS321 capture to explain the clock phases it reproduces.

badges.title: Tank Battalion
badges.reason: The core models the Tank Battalion board as TTL chips at their board positions, such as the 74LS139 at C3. Its engine, shot and hit sounds are fixed-point models of the board's analog circuits taken from the PCB schematic, down to parts such as R58, R60, R61 and C13 (commit by shimian5).

badges.title: Off the Wall
badges.reason: Built from Atari's schematics and the equations of the board's GAL chips (136090-1003, -1006, -1007 and the JSA III's 136085-1038 and -1039), with MAME only as a cross-reference where the published documents are silent. The README lists which sections follow the schematics and where Atari's own sheets were never published.

badges.title: Relief Pitcher
badges.reason: Built from the schematic sheets in Atari's TM-376 manual and the logic read from the board's GAL chips. MAME 0.289 served only as a reference where those are silent.

badges.title: Shuuz
badges.reason: Built from the schematics in Atari's TM-358 manual and the board's dumped GALs, with MAME 0.289 only as a cross-check and as the source for the unpublished video chips. RTL comments name board parts by PCB location, such as the 74LS163A at 50B, and signals by their schematic names.

badges.title: Armed Police Batrider
badges.reason: Pramod Somashekar reverse engineered part of the Armed Police Batrider (RA9704) board's schematic for his Verilog implementation of it. The Coin-Op Collection team later published a full reverse-engineered RA9704 schematic and PCB layout by Brandon Arnold, which credits that partial schematic.

badges.title: Mahou Daisakusen
badges.reason: The core's author, Pramod Somashekar, writes that atrac17 traced the Z80 sound sections of the Sorcer Striker and Kingdom Grandprix boards to fix the sound speed in these games. That trace showed the Z80 WAIT signal comes from the YM2151's inverted DOUT pin, which the core follows.

badges.title: Zero Wing
badges.reason: Verified against an OutZone conversion running on a Zero Wing (TP-015) board, loaned by @owlnonymous; the timing of that board was captured with a DSLogic logic analyzer. The core was built from the OutZone (TP-018) schematics in its repository.

badges.title: Truxton II
badges.reason: atrac17 developed the core with Toaplan V2 hardware loaned by @90s_cyber_thriller. Its README gives the Tatsujin Oh (TP-024) board's sync rates as measured with a DSLogic logic analyzer, and photos of that board are in its doc folder. atrac17's own Toaplan2 repository is gone; the links point to a public copy that holds his commits.

badges.title: Cadash (rmCores)
badges.reason: On a real Cadash board the sprites shift slightly while the screen scrolls; the rmCores README says this was confirmed on a genuine PCB, that MAME does not reproduce it, and offers it as a Cadash-only option because Cadash is the board the evidence comes from. This is the same evidence as the Distribution Cadash entry, stated in this core's own repository.

badges.title: Seibu Cup Soccer (rmCores)
badges.reason: Checked against an original Seibu Cup Soccer board (SYS68C2). The rmCores README quotes the board's owner, who had never seen the core, judging its coprocessor-driven play in line with the PCB, and shows photos of the board the findings were checked against.

badges.title: The Legend of Kage (Rev 2) [CoC]
badges.reason: The core's author traced the Taito A54 board set into schematics and built the core from them. The video timings were taken from the PCB, and the sound section's control curves were matched against a recording of the PCB.

badges.title: The Lost Castle In Darkmist
badges.reason: Built against the author's own Lost Castle in Darkmist (SEI-8608) board, with footage from it in the release post; the audio output chain was modelled stage by stage from the board's schematic.

badges.title: Bubble Bobble (Japan, Ver 0.1) [CoC]
badges.reason: The core's timings were taken from the schematic and the author's PCB, the microcontroller interrupt delay was measured on the PCB (about 96 us after vertical blank), and the release post shows the core and the PCB running side by side.

badges.title: KiKi KaiKai

badges.title: Wardner

badges.title: Mystic Warriors
